title: turbo-tasks: add lazy cell reads via LazyReadRef
body:
### What?

Adds `vc.lazy_reader().await?`, which returns a `LazyReadRef<T>` for any value type. The value is only accessible through an explicit `LazyReadRef::get()`.

- While the ref is alive, the task depends on the whole cell, so invalidations during the execution are not lost.
- If the ref is dropped without `get()` ever being called, the dependency registered by this read is removed. That proves the task doesn't depend on the cell.
- If `get()` was called, the dependency is kept and becomes a normal full dependency when the execution completes.

Stacked on #100884 and reuses its `CellKey::Keyed(id)` machinery.

### Why?

Some tasks need a cell's value only in rare cases, and only find out in synchronous code. One example is the server actions hash salt (encryption key) in #100950: today that needs an optimistic "run without it, bail, re-run with it" strategy. With `lazy_reader()`, the task can read the cell up front, pass the ref into synchronous code, and depend on it only when it is actually used.

### How?

- **One dependency per read:** every `lazy_reader()` call gets its own `CellKey::Keyed(id)` dependency edge, the same per-execution id that `keyed()` uses.
  - Dropping an unaccessed ref calls `convert_keyed_cell_dependency` with no key hashes, which removes only that edge.
  - Full reads (`.await`), hashed/keyed reads (`get`, `contains_key`, `keyed()`), and other `LazyReadRef`s of the same cell keep their own edges. Mixed reads in one execution therefore behave correctly, in any order.
  - An accessed ref leaves its `Keyed` edge in place. The existing completion-time conversion turns it into a normal full dependency.
- **Lifetime rules:** the same as `KeyedReadRef`, sharing the alive-ref counter. A ref that is leaked or dropped outside the creating execution fails the task with a panic error, and its dependency is kept as a full dependency.
  - In debug builds, a cross-execution `poll`, `get()` or `drop` also panics at the misuse site.
  - In release builds, the conservative full dependency is kept.
- **Reused race handling:** the missing-content guard in `convert_keyed_cell_dependency` and the `update_cell` handling from #100884 also apply to removal.
- **Untracked reads:** `vc.untracked().lazy_reader()` stays untracked and never registers a removable edge.
- **No cost for other tasks:** tasks that use neither `keyed()` nor `lazy_reader()` don't pay anything new. The completion scan and leak check stay gated on the existing per-execution counter.
- `keyed()` and `lazy_reader()` share one read helper. `keyed()` behaviour is unchanged.
  - The only exception is the leak panic message, which now names both `KeyedReadRef` and `LazyReadRef`.
- The new rule is documented in `turbopack/AGENTS.md` next to the `keyed()` guidance.

Adopting this in the server actions transform is a separate follow-up.

### Verification

- New `turbopack/crates/turbo-tasks-backend/tests/lazy_read_ref.rs` (17 tests) covers:
  - unaccessed vs accessed reads, and a cell change while the ref is alive;
  - two lazy refs (one or none accessed, both drop orders);
  - an unaccessed lazy read combined with a full read before or while the ref is alive;
  - lazy plus keyed `get()` and lazy plus batched `keyed()` reads;
  - access flipping between executions;
  - drops in a detached future;
  - leaked or cross-thread refs failing the task while keeping the dependency;
  - cross-execution misuse panicking in debug only;
  - untracked lazy reads;
  - `Debug` not counting as an access;
  - reads outside a task.
- `cargo test -p turbo-tasks -p turbo-tasks-backend` passes, including the existing `keyed_read_ref.rs`.
- `cargo test --release -p turbo-tasks-backend --test lazy_read_ref --test keyed_read_ref` passes, covering the release-mode fallback paths.
- Mutation checks, each reverted afterwards:
  - keeping unaccessed dependencies → 5 failures;
  - removing accessed dependencies → 4 failures;
  - removing other full edges of the same cell → 3 failures;
  - ignoring `.untracked()` → 1 failure.
- `cargo clippy -p turbo-tasks -p turbo-tasks-backend --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items -p turbo-tasks -p turbo-tasks-backend` pass.
- Not run locally: the workspace-wide `./scripts/check-rustdoc.sh`, and Next.js e2e tests (no consumer is converted in this PR).

title: fix: exclude non-prefetchable cache entries from RDC
body:
This PR fixes an issue where non-prefetchable cache entries were still being included in the Resume Data Cache (RDC), even though they were already excluded from the prerendered result.

The issue happened because the RDC serializer wasn't checking the stale value against MIN_PREFETCHABLE_STALE.

I've updated the serializer to exclude these entries as well, keeping its behavior consistent with the prerendering logic.

Testing

- Added an E2E regression test for non-prefetchable cache entries.

- Verified that the test fails without the fix and passes after applying it.

- Ran the use-cache E2E test suite in start mode (59 tests passed).

Fixes #100982

title: feat(turbopack): Add EmitOption trait for extensible chunking context configuration
body:
Recreates #92807 (by @sokra) on top of current `canary`, which it no longer merges into cleanly. Supersedes #92807.

### What?

Replaces the `MinifyType` / `MangleType` enums and `ChunkingContext::minify_type()` with an extensible `EmitOption` marker-trait system. Each crate now defines its own emit options: `EcmascriptEmitOptions` (full SWC `MinifyOptions`, `indent`, `merged_module_comments`) and `CssEmitOptions` (`minify`, `chunk_item_comments`). Chunking contexts store a heterogeneous `Vec<ResolvedVc<Box<dyn EmitOption>>>`. Consumers look up their option type and fall back to defaults when it's missing.

### Why?

`MinifyType` ties `turbopack-core` to specific minification strategies. Passing full SWC minify options through it would mean adding `swc_core` as a dependency of `turbopack-core`. With `EmitOption`, each crate owns its own options without that coupling.

### How?

This is the design from #92807. The changes below adapt it to current canary and address the outstanding review comments.

**Review comments from #92807 addressed**
- `ChunkingContext::emit_options()` no longer has a default impl. All implementors (`BrowserChunkingContext`, `NodeJsChunkingContext`, `UseCacheContentHashChunkingContext`) implement it explicitly.
- `process_parse_result` takes `&EcmascriptEmitOptions` instead of the `indent` / `merged_module_comments` booleans.

**Adapted to canary**
- The chunk version is now the shared `turbopack-ecmascript/src/hmr/version.rs` (browser + node). It stores `ReadRef<EcmascriptEmitOptions>` and hashes it with `deterministic_hash()`.
- The xxh3 `std::hash::Hasher` adapter normalizes integer writes to fixed-width little-endian. That keeps the input bytes for the standard presets independent of the build host's byte order and pointer width.
- Migrated callers that appeared after #92807: `UseCacheContentHashChunkingContext` (next-api), the service worker chunking context, and the browser runtime chunk.
- Migrated six newer snapshot fixtures from `minifyType` to `minifyMode`.
- Updated `turbo_tasks` attributes to current syntax (`serialization = "skip"`, `unsafe_ignore`).

Emitted output is unchanged: presets keep 2 compress passes, the reserved `AbortSignal`, deterministic mangling for SSR/edge, and preserved names when mangling is off.

### Verification

- `cargo test -p turbopack-tests --test snapshot`: 134 passed, no snapshot output changes
- `cargo test -p turbopack-tests --test execution`: 322 passed
- `cargo test -p turbopack-ecmascript --lib emit_options`: new test, preset hashes are distinct and reproducible
- `cargo check --workspace --tests`, `cargo clippy` on the touched crates, `cargo fmt --check`
- Not verified: cross-architecture hash equality for arbitrary custom SWC options. SWC's `GlobalDefs` hashes internally with `FxHasher`. The standard presets don't set it.

title: [ci] Add scheduled future compatibility checks for deprecations
body:
Add an opt-in `futureCompat` mode to build-and-test and deploy-release so Node.js deprecations surface as failures before they become breaking changes. This frame keeps the existing Node.js versions. The next frame selects latest Node.js.

- Enable the mode automatically on Sundays at 07:17 UTC for build-and-test and 10:17 UTC for deploy-release. Scheduled deployments resolve one exact `next@canary` version for all shards.
- Enforce `--throw-deprecation` through the test harness, including fixture and per-call Node options, custom commands, and deployment builds and functions. Preserve the existing child-only pending-deprecation behavior.
- Disable build and passed-test result cache reuse in future mode so checks actually execute. Manual and scheduled runs use full-suite semantics rather than changed-test detection.

title: turbopack: share module source map tails across module factories
body:
Stacked on #99969.

### What?

Module source maps are now stored once per module, rather than once per module factory.

A module's map is split into:

- a small **head**: `version`, `file` and `sources`
- a **tail** `Rope` cell owned by the module-content task, holding every byte after `sources`

Each module factory rewrites only the head's `sources`. Its section-map cell is a `CellRope` made of that rewritten head inline, followed by a reference to the module's tail cell. Chunk source maps nest these factory map ropes. Maps that aren't split (raw maps, minified-factory maps, maps built elsewhere) are stored inline in the `CellRope`, with the same bytes as before.

`.js` and `.js.map` output are unchanged, and the JSON field order of the maps is unchanged.

### Why?

`sources` is the only part of a module's map that differs between that module's factories (one factory per chunking context and async variant). The bytes after it are identical across factories, and they are most of the map: `sourcesContent`, `names` and `mappings`.

Before this change, every factory persisted a full flattened copy of the module's map. The module content also kept the full map inline, so the same bytes were persisted roughly once per factory plus once more.

### How?

- **`StructuredSourceMap`:**
  - `to_rope` is now split into head and tail writers, so `split()` returns the head plus the serialized tail.
  - `head_to_rope()` followed by the tail reproduces `to_rope()` exactly.
  - The tail also completes a head whose `sources` were rewritten: rewriting never changes which head fields are present, so the separating comma stays correct.
- **`SplitSourceMap`:** a head plus a tail `ResolvedVc<Rope>`. It is used by `EcmascriptModuleContent` and `EcmascriptChunkItemContent`.
- **`SectionMap::Split`:** this is how a factory's `Code` carries its map. `Code` is hash-only, so the in-memory value also keeps the tail bytes for code that reads the map synchronously. `Code::resolved_code_cells` persists only the inline head plus the tail reference.
- **`CodeCells`:** section maps are `CellRope` cells. Reading a factory's code back (`CodeCells::to_code`) reads them, and `CodeComposition::generate_source_map` references them as nested ropes.
- **Minimal adaptations:**
  - the raw module and CSS runtime chunk items split their maps;
  - `StaticEcmascriptCode` reassembles its module's map.

### Results

On `bench/nested-deps-app-router-many-pages`, comparing #99969's head (`662113726a`) against this change. Both binaries were release builds without LTO, with `print_cache_item_size_with_compressed`.

**Output equivalence.** Every emitted file is byte-identical between base and change:

| Mode | Steps compared | Files per step |
|---|---|---:|
| dev | cold, no edit, second no edit, leaf edit, page edit | 167 |
| prod, `turbopackMinifyBeforeChunking: true` | the same five steps | 2,652 |
| prod, whole-chunk minification | cold | 2,652 |

**Dev cold session, persisted task data.** Both runs persisted 61,335 module factory tasks and 9,752 `EcmascriptModuleContent::new` tasks.

| Task | Base raw | Change raw | Base lz4 | Change lz4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `module_factory_with_code_generation_issue` | 344.5 MiB | 219.0 MiB | 129.8 MiB | 79.4 MiB |
| `EcmascriptModuleContent::new` | 47.7 MiB | 47.6 MiB | 20.6 MiB | 20.1 MiB |

Factory task data drops by about 36% raw and 39% lz4. Module content tasks stay the same size: their tail moves into a cell of the same task, so nothing is persisted twice.

The cache directory after the cold session went from 275.0 MB to 254.5 MB. That's one run per arm, and the base wrote two snapshots while the change wrote one, so I don't compare whole-session totals. Two other base cold sessions didn't snapshot at all and are excluded (see the follow-up below).

**Prod build, per-item minification on.** Two interleaved runs per binary:

| | Base | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Peak RSS | 1,480 / 1,451 MiB | 1,474 / 1,404 MiB |
| Wall time | 24.0 / 24.2 s | 23.0 / 24.3 s |
| Persistent cache | 167.0 / 167.0 MB | 165.9 / 165.8 MB |

The prod effect is small, as expected. Minified factories have their own maps, with rewritten `names` and `mappings`, and those are still stored inline. Peak RSS is the largest single child process, and two runs aren't enough for a memory claim.

### Tests

- **`turbopack-core` unit tests:**
  - head + tail reassembly is byte-identical to `to_rope()`, before and after `sources` rewriting, for swc maps with and without `sourcesContent`, raw and undecodable input maps, maps without `sources`, an empty head, a head-only map and an index map;
  - factory map cells reference the module tail and read as the old flat map, and unsplit structured and raw maps stay inline;
  - a tail-only edit updates the composed map without re-running the composition or changing factory map values.
- **`turbopack-core` persistence test:** tail edits after restores, including one after the final restore, keep the composition and factory map cells stable and write the new map bytes.
- **Existing suites:** Turbopack snapshot (136) and execution (325) tests pass without updating any snapshots.

### Follow-ups

- **Minification and persistence:** persisting reference-only per-item minification values, and sharing `sourcesContent` in minified factory maps.
- **Dev snapshots:** cold dev sessions sometimes never write a snapshot.

title: Don't let a navigation wait on an in-flight loading-boundary prefetch
body:
Fixes #100968

### What

A navigation that starts while the target's default prefetch (up to the loading boundary) is still in flight can't commit until that prefetch lands, even if its own response started arriving long before. The URL doesn't change and `loading.js` isn't shown until then.

### Why

In `createRenderTreeForSegment`, a `Pending` segment cache entry is adopted as the segment's data. If the entry is expected to come back `FullyComplete`, the segment is also left out of the navigation request, so the only thing that can fill it is the prefetch. The segment that owns the loading boundary and the head render outside any Suspense boundary, so the whole transition suspends on the prefetch promise.

How this came to bite the default link:

- Since 16.3.1-canary.16 (#96788) the non-PPR tree prefetch response no longer carries the head and the segments up to the loading boundary; they come from the separate legacy prefetch request, which the reporter's harness delays. The head is spawned there as a full prefetch, whose pending entry is marked complete and skipped from the navigation request. That's what the reporter saw on 16.4.3: the head alone blocks.
- #99706 replaced `fetchStrategy` with `stage` + `completeness`, and the loading-boundary prefetch now spawns its segment entries as `Navigation`/`FullyComplete` as well (before, they were `LoadingBoundary`, i.e. partial). On canary the `target` segment blocks the same way as the head.

### How

Pending entries spawned by a loading-boundary prefetch get `isLoadingBoundaryPrefetch`, and the navigation treats them as partial: it requests those segments and the head itself, and renders the prefetched data only if it lands first (`prefetchRsc`). This is the path every partial pending entry already takes.

A legacy full prefetch (`prefetch={true}` or `prefetch="navigation"`) keeps the existing behaviour: the navigation waits for it instead of requesting the same segments again (`force-stale` has a test for that). I first tried treating every pending entry as partial; that broke that test, hence the flag.

Why a flag rather than spawning those entries as `CacheComplete` (which is what the pre-#99706 `isPartial` amounted to): the head is pinged as `Navigation`/`FullyComplete` on both legacy paths, so a `CacheComplete` pending head would fail `doesEntrySatisfyPrefetch` for the next task and spawn a duplicate head revalidation, and `isExistingSegmentEntryPreferred` would rank it below any fulfilled entry. The flag leaves the cache's own bookkeeping alone and only changes what the navigation does with an in-flight entry. A per-task property doesn't work because `createRenderTreeForSegment` only sees the entry.

The commit itself comes from React's deferred lane: the transition render still suspends on the prefetch promise (`prefetchRsc`), and the deferred render of `rsc` commits once the navigation response arrives. So `loading.js` appears at the first navigation chunk, not at click.

Tradeoffs:

- A click that lands during an in-flight loading-boundary prefetch of the same route requests the segments above the boundary and the head again, which the pre-#99706 code did for the segments. For the head that's new: when everything else is cached, the navigation sends a metadata-only request where before it sent nothing, so `generateMetadata` can run twice for that click.
- With `optimisticRouting` (default) a pending head takes the existing "render an empty head until the response arrives" path instead of blocking, so title and meta are blank for the transition window.
- A pending loading-boundary prefetch that gets rejected (404, rendered-search mismatch) used to suspend that segment until the router re-rendered; now the navigation response fills it.
- Not covered: under Cache Components a static per-segment prefetch of a fully static route is also `Pending`/`FullyComplete` and awaited, so a slow one still holds a click the same way. Likewise `experimental.dynamicOnHover` upgrades a default link to a full prefetch on hover, so a click in that window waits for it. Both are the same "wait for a full prefetch" convention and I left them alone.

## Summary

The TypeScript, decorators and JSX transform options each walked the tsconfig `extends` chain over raw JSON, one accessor per option. They now read one typed `TsConfigCompilerOptions` cell instead. title: Turbopack: read package.json main and alias fields through typed projections
body:
## Summary

When resolving into a package, the main fields (`main`, `module`, ...) and the alias field (`browser`) were read straight from the parsed `package.json`. Any edit to that file, such as to `scripts` or `dependencies`, therefore invalidated those resolutions.

They now go through per-field tasks, like the `exports` and `imports` fields already do:
- `package_json_string_field(path, field)` returns the field's string
- `package_json_alias_field(path, field)` returns the alias entries as typed values: `false` means ignore, a string is a request to resolve instead, and anything else is kept as JSON text for the existing error

Resolution now depends only on these small cells, so an edit to an unrelated field stops at them. Behavior is unchanged, including the "invalid alias field value" issue.

### What?

Add general e2e coverage for sitemap regeneration after a time-based revalidation interval, `revalidateTag`, and `revalidatePath`.

### Why?

Existing metadata tests check response shape, prerender settings, and build outputs, but do not verify that a deployed sitemap actually refreshes. ### Summary

Please backport #99743 ("Resolve relative imports in `next.config.ts` from the config directory", `c632caf`, merged to `canary` on 2026-10-13) to the maintained **15.5.x** line. It fixes #99742.

- **What it fixes:** with the default SWC loader, `next.config.ts` is compiled in memory by `requireFromString`, which never sets the module's `filename`. Relative imports in the config therefore resolve against `process.cwd()` instead of the config's directory, so loading the config from any other directory fails, or silently loads a different file if one exists at the cwd-relative path.
- **Where the fix is today:** it is in `16.5.0-canary.28`. It is not in `15.5.28` (the current `backport` tag) or `16.4.3`, and I found no backport PR.

title: Turbopack: use simd-utf16-len for source position column counting
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #100919. `SourcePos::update` uses the local `utf16_len` helper to count the UTF-16 length of the last line segment. This PR backs that helper with the SIMD kernels of [`simd-utf16-len`](https://github.com/SyMind/simd-utf16-len) 0.3.1. The new crate computes the same per-byte formula. Continuation bytes count 0, 4-byte leaders count 2, and every other byte counts 1. The gain matters most on long lines such as minified code. In an earlier synthetic micro-benchmark, a minified one-liner scanned roughly 7–8× faster than with the plain byte loop.

The crate currently only accepts `&str`, while rope chunks are `&[u8]`. The helper therefore converts with `from_utf8_unchecked`, in an `unsafe` block with this justification:

- `utf16_len` doesn't depend on UTF-8 validity for memory safety. All of its loads are bounded by the slice length, and byte values only affect the count. The crate's internal `# Safety` comments say that UTF-8 is required for safety, but that isn't true; it is only needed for correctness. The crate's maintainer [describes valid UTF-8 as needed "to produce a meaningful UTF-16 length"](https://github.com/SyMind/simd-utf16-len/pull/22#issuecomment-6514541196).
- On targets without SIMD, the crate falls back to `str::encode_utf16().count()`. std specializes `EncodeUtf16::count` as a byte-wise fold that doesn't decode chars, so the same reasoning holds there.
- This was checked against `simd-utf16-len` 0.3.1 (pinned in `Cargo.lock`) and the pinned toolchain. Re-check before upgrading either.

A TODO tracks switching to the crate's byte-slice API once https://github.com/SyMind/simd-utf16-len/pull/22 lands, which removes the `unsafe`.

The helper's own unit tests are dropped. The `SourcePos` tests still cover the column semantics.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p turbopack-core --lib`
- Reviewed the crate's x86_64, aarch64 and wasm32 kernels, its ASCII-prefix helpers and its scalar fallback for loads that depend on byte values. There are none outside tests.
- Ran the crate under Miri (x86_64) on malformed inputs of 1–320 bytes at several offsets, comparing against the per-byte formula and `encode_utf16().count()`.

title: Soft navigation waits for the target's in-flight segment prefetch (page head) instead of showing loading.js (regression in 16.3.1-canary.16, still in 16.4.3)

labels.name: Linking and Navigating
labels.description: Related to Next.js linking (e.g., <Link>) and navigation.

labels.name: Loading UI and Streaming
labels.description: Related to loading UI (loading.tsx) and streaming.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/timson-js/next-head-blocks-navigation-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`, then `npm run build && npm start` (serves on `http://localhost:3100`).
2. In another terminal, run `node measure.mjs 5` (Playwright, Chromium).
   - The script opens `/`, which has a single `<Link href="/target">` with the default prefetch.
   - It waits until the `/_tree` prefetch for `/target` has arrived, then clicks the link while
     the segment-data prefetch for `/target` is still in flight.
   - To make that window deterministic, it delays only non-`/_tree` prefetch requests by 3 s,
     standing in for a slow network or a busy prefetch queue. The navigation request is not delayed.
3. The script prints, per click, the time until the URL changes, until `app/target/loading.js`
   is shown, and until the page content is shown.

`/target` is dynamic (`await connection()` plus a 1.2 s delay) and has its own `loading.js`.
The root layout exports a static `metadata`. There is no other config.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected** (and what 16.3.8 does): the click commits right away. The URL changes and
`loading.js` is shown within about 70 ms, then the page replaces it once the navigation
response arrives, about 1.2 s later.

**Current** (16.3.1-canary.16 through 16.4.3 and 16.5.0-canary.34): nothing happens on screen
until the delayed **prefetch** resolves. The URL stays on `/`, `loading.js` is never shown,
and the page appears only when the prefetch finishes, even though the navigation response
arrived after about 1.2 s.

Five runs each, `PREFETCH_DELAY_MS=3000`:

| `next`           | URL change (median) | `loading.js` shown | content (median) |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------- |
| 16.3.8           | 71 ms               | 5/5                | 1242 ms          |
| 16.4.3           | 2748 ms             | 0/5                | 2748 ms          |
| 16.5.0-canary.34 | 2741 ms             | 0/5                | 2741 ms          |

With a 6 s prefetch delay, 16.4.3 commits after about 5.75 s. The wait follows the prefetch,
not the navigation response.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0
  Available memory (MB): 16384
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 22.18.0
  npm: 11.7.0
  Yarn: 1.22.19
  pnpm: 8.15.9
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.3 // Latest available version is detected (16.4.3).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.1
  react-dom: 19.3.1
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Linking and Navigating, Loading UI and Streaming, Metadata

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local), Other (Deployed)

### Additional context

**Bisect** (two runs per version):

| `next`           | result                     |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- |
| 16.3.1-canary.15 | good: 102 ms, loading shown |
| 16.3.1-canary.16 | bad: 2739 ms               |

The first bad release is `16.3.1-canary.16`. Its changelog contains the client cache refactors
#96788, #96876, #96877 and #96878 (tree and per-segment prefetches converted to
`NavigationFlightResponse`, unified cache writes) and a React upgrade (#97249).

**Where it waits.** With logging added in `next/dist`, the router takes the soft-navigation
path immediately: the route tree is cached, so it runs `navigateUsingPrefetchedRouteTree` →
`completeSoftNavigation` within a few ms of the click. The commit is then held by the page
head. The head is a separate segment-cache entry that is still `Pending`, because it travels
with the delayed segment prefetch. `Head` in `client/components/app-router.js` returns
`useDeferredValue(head, prefetchHead)`, which here is a pending promise rendered outside any
Suspense boundary, so React suspends the whole transition until the prefetch resolves.

As a control experiment, I patched `Head` to return `null` while its promise is pending. The
same scenario on 16.4.3 then commits in 72 ms (3/3) and shows `loading.js`.

**Impact.** In a real app with many links per page (dozens of prefetches, 4 at a time), a click
in the first seconds after load routinely lands in this window. The link appears to do nothing
until the target's prefetch completes. It reproduces on a fast local machine; it does not need
CPU contention.

**Related:** #100436 ("Link click never commits when the navigation starts during the target's
metadata-only prefetch", 16.2.6). Similar trigger, a click while the target's metadata is
still being prefetched. There the navigation never commits; here it commits only when the
prefetch finishes.

title: turbo-tasks: add OrderedJsonValue/OrderedJsonMap with key-order-sensitive equality
body:
## Summary

Adds `turbo_tasks::OrderedJsonValue` and `turbo_tasks::OrderedJsonMap`. These are the JSON counterparts of the ordered index collections from #100940: wrappers around `serde_json::Value`/`Map` whose `PartialEq`/`Eq` and `Hash` follow object key order. It also moves the JSON values whose consumers read key order onto them.

**Why:** `serde_json` compares and hashes objects ignoring key order. With `preserve_order`, which our build enables through feature unification, `Map`'s `Hash` sorts the entries first. That is consistent with "JSON objects are unordered", but some of our consumers read the order:
- `package.json` `exports`/`imports` conditions are matched in key order, first match wins. Reordering them compared equal, so the cell kept the old content and resolution kept the old priority until the cache was cleared.
- Loader and plugin options are passed to JavaScript, where key order is observable (a PostCSS `plugins` object is applied in key order, for example).

The webpack-loader and swc-plugin option types also hashed `serde_json::to_string(...)`, which follows order, while deriving the order-insensitive `Eq`. They now derive `Hash` from the ordered wrapper, so `Hash` and `Eq` agree.

The wrappers:
- `Deref` to the inner `Value`/`Map`, so readers don't change
- pass serde through, and bincode through `turbo_bincode::serde_self_describing` (key order survives persistence)
- implement `ShrinkToFit`
- are registered as `NonLocalValue`/`OperationValue`, and `OrderedJsonValue` is also a primitive cell type next to `serde_json::Value`

Migrated:
- `FileJsonContent::Content`, plus `FileJsonContent::content()`, which now returns `Vc<OrderedJsonValue>`. That cell was the same hazard one step downstream, and the PostCSS config loader reads it.
- `WebpackLoaderItem.options`, `ResolvedWebpackLoaderItem.options`, and the swc-plugin `JsonValue`
- `NextConfig.output_file_tracing_includes` / `excludes`

`turbo-tasks` now enables `serde_json/preserve_order` itself. It was already on in every real build; without it, objects are sorted by key and the order carries no information.

## Verification

- New tests:
  - unit tests: reordered (also nested) objects compare and hash differently, and a bincode round trip keeps the order
  - `turbopack-core` `test_exports_conditions_reorder`: rewrites `package.json` with the `exports` conditions reordered within one session and checks that `exports_field` returns the new order. With order-insensitive equality it fails (`["import", "default"]` instead of `["default", "import"]`).
- `cargo check --workspace --tests`, and `cargo clippy --tests` for `turbo-tasks`, `turbo-tasks-fs`, `turbopack-core`, `turbopack-ecmascript`, `turbopack-node`, `next-core`: clean
- Lib tests:
  - `turbo-tasks`, `next-core`: pass
  - `turbo-tasks-fs`: 11 symlink and denied-path tests fail on macOS, and the same 11 fail on the base branch
  - `turbopack-core`: the 25 `resolve::` temp-dir tests fail identically on the base branch; everything else passes
- Not run: Next.js integration tests

title: fix(app-render): stop prerendered Link headers from accumulating on revalidation
body: ### What? With `cacheComponents: true`, a `Link` header set in `next.config.js` `headers()` (or by middleware) is duplicated on ISR pages that also emit a React preload `Link` (e.g. an ``), and gains one more copy on every background revalidation: ``` req 3 Link: ; rel="llms-txt" Link: ; rel="llms-txt",; rel="llms-txt",; rel=preload; as="image"; fetchpriority="high" req 4 Link: ; rel="llms-txt" Link: ; rel="llms-txt",; rel="llms-txt",; rel="llms-txt",; rel=preload; ... ... ``` An on-demand render (cache `MISS`) of a page not prerendered at build time also returns both the config `Link` and the preload `Link` twice. ### Why? `prerenderToStream` handles React's `onHeaders` by appending each value to the live response and then storing `res.getHeader(name)` in `metadata.headers`, which becomes the APP_PAGE cache entry's `headers`. That snapshot includes values the render did not produce: - the `Link` from `headers()` in next.config.js, already on the response before rendering; - during a background revalidation, the `Link` values the serving path replayed from the previous cache entry onto the same response. `app-page-runtime` appends the cache entry's headers to every response after the config headers are set, so each regeneration stores, and later serves, one more copy. On a `MISS` the render has already written the headers to the response, and the same values are appended again from `metadata.headers`. ### How? `prerenderToStream` now records only the values it produces (React's `onHeaders` output and the redirect `location`) in `metadata.headers`, and no longer writes them to the response. Every consumer of a prerender result already applies `metadata.headers` to the response (`app-page-runtime` for fresh renders and cache hits, the export worker at build time), so the headers reach the client exactly once. A `Link` from middleware or next.config.js is still merged with React's preload `Link` (#73431), because the cached value is appended to the response, not set over it. `renderToStream` (the dynamic path) is unchanged. It writes `onHeaders` output to the response only and never stores it in `metadata.headers`, so it has no cache entry to accumulate into. Added `test/production/app-dir/cache-components-link-header`, which configures a `Link` in `headers()`, renders a `'use cache'` page with a 1s `revalidate` and a high-priority image, and checks the config `Link` and the preload `Link` appear exactly once on every response across four revalidations, for a build-time prerendered page, a prerendered dynamic param, and an on-demand dynamic param. Without the change it fails on webpack (the config `Link` count climbs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and the `MISS` response has 2 of each). With the change it passes on both webpack and Turbopack. One behavioural difference: the segment-prefetch cache branch returns before the cached headers are replayed, so an RSC segment-prefetch response that happens to trigger a fresh render no longer carries the preload `Link`. Such responses have no use for a preload. Standalone reproduction: https://github.com/linyiru/next-cache-components-link-header-repro Fixes #100959

body: ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/linyiru/next-cache-components-link-header-repro ### To Reproduce 1. `git clone https://github.com/linyiru/next-cache-components-link-header-repro && cd next-cache-components-link-header-repro` 2. `npm install && npm run build && npm start` 3. In another terminal, run `./scripts/probe.sh`. It requests `/` every 3s and counts the copies of the `Link` value set in `next.config.js` `headers()`. The app has `cacheComponents: true`, a `Link` header on `/` from `headers()`, and a `'use cache'` page with `cacheLife({ stale: 300, revalidate: 2, expire: 3600 })` that renders one ``. ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Expected:** every response carries the configured `Link` value once. **Current:** the configured value is duplicated, and gains one more copy on every background regeneration, with no upper bound: ``` request 1: llms-txt copies=1 x-nextjs-cache: HIT request 2: llms-txt copies=1 x-nextjs-cache: STALE request 3: llms-txt copies=2 x-nextjs-cache: STALE request 4: llms-txt copies=3 x-nextjs-cache: STALE ... request 8: llms-txt copies=7 x-nextjs-cache: STALE Link: ; rel="llms-txt" Link: ; rel="llms-txt",; rel="llms-txt",…(×7),; rel=preload; as="image"; fetchpriority="high" ``` In production, one of our storefront pages had reached 28 copies (12 KB of response headers) a few hours after a deploy. It would keep growing until a proxy or browser header-size limit rejects the response. The bug needs all of these: - `cacheComponents: true`. Without it, a plain `export const revalidate = 2` page stays at 1 copy. - A `Link` header from `next.config.js` `headers()`. - React emitting a resource-hint `Link` header (here, from a high-priority image). - A background regeneration (ISR). **Cause.** In `packages/next/src/server/app-render/app-render.tsx`, the headers that end up in the APP_PAGE cache entry are recorded like this: ```js const setMetadataHeader = (name) => { metadata.headers ??= {} metadata.headers[name] = res.getHeader(name) } ``` `appendHeader` and `setHeader` call it after writing to `res`. React's `onHeaders` (passed through `createOnHeadersCallback(appendHeader)` in the `cacheComponents` prerender path) appends its preload `Link`. At that point `res.getHeader('link')` returns the **whole** value on the response: the copy from `next.config.js` `headers()`, plus, during a background revalidation, the copies the serving path already replayed from the stale entry. All of that is stored in the new entry. The serving path in `app-page.ts` then `appendHeader`s `cachedData.headers` after the config headers, so each regeneration adds one more copy. **Workaround:** `reactMaxHeadersLength: 0` (commented out in the repro's `next.config.js`). React then emits no `Link` header and the count stays at 1. The preload hints still ship as `` in ``. **Suggested fix:** record only the values the render itself set or appended, instead of reading back `res.getHeader(name)`. ### Provide environment information ```bash Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0 Available memory (MB): 32768 Available CPU cores: 12 Binaries: Node: 22.23.4 npm: 10.9.9 Yarn: 1.22.22 pnpm: 12.11.2 Relevant Packages: next: 16.4.3 // Latest available version is detected (16.4.3). eslint-config-next: N/A react: 19.2.9 react-dom: 19.2.9 typescript: N/A Next.js Config: output: N/A ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) cacheComponents, Headers, Use Cache ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) next start (local), Other (Deployed) ### Additional context - Also reproduces on `16.5.0-canary.34`. Its `app-render.js` contains the same `setMetadataHeader`. - Seen first on 16.4.2 in production: self-hosted `next start` with a custom `cacheHandler`. The handler stores entries verbatim, and the repro uses the default handler. - A fix PR with an e2e test will follow and link here.

title: fix(next): read server HMR pull from one coherent operation
body:
### What?

Server HMR pulls in Turbopack dev now take the snapshot, the output file writes, the per-chunk-list diff and the next baseline from **one** strongly consistent operation, instead of two separate `turbo_tasks.run`s.

### Why?

`project_get_server_hmr_update` used to work in two steps:
1. Read `server_hmr_snapshot_with_effects_operation` (chunk lists, version `to`, issues, effects) and apply its effects.
2. In a second run, diff each chunk list through its own root operation, `compute_update_from_version_operation(content, from)`.

The diff operations only *read* the chunk-list content cells. Their producers weren't part of the diff's call tree. Strong consistency only covers an operation's own call tree, so during lazy activation a diff could read transient content while a producer was still settling. The two runs could also see different states, so a diff might not match the files the first run wrote. JS then stored the snapshot's `to` as the new baseline.

With `turbopackLazyDynamicImports` and `turbopackLazyDynamicImportsSSR` enabled, this shows up as an SSR `ChunkLoadError` for a lazy-compilation proxy chunk that was never written. After that, every page falls back to client rendering. It's timing dependent and appears mainly under CPU load.

### How?

- New `server_hmr_update_with_effects_operation(project, entry_paths, from: TransientInstance<Option<ServerHmrPullBaseline>>)`:
  - it connects the existing (shared, cached) snapshot-with-effects operation and diffs with plain child task calls;
  - so everything the diff reads is in the call tree of the operation that is read strongly consistently;
  - the pull reads it once with `read_strongly_consistent_and_apply_effects`, so the effects, `to`, issues and update all come from the same settled execution.
- `ServerHmrPullBaseline` is built once per pull outside Turbo Tasks. It holds one `TransientInstance` per chunk-list version, so the diff task keys stay stable while the pull settles and are never shared between pulls.
  - Once the pull's top-level task finishes, old baselines are not diffed again.
- A pull **without** a baseline (e.g. the first pull after a restart) has nothing to diff. It reads the shared snapshot operation directly, once, strongly consistently, and returns `NoRuntimeUpdate { to }`. So it doesn't create a per-pull task, and the warm-restart task statistics are unchanged.
- The snapshot operation stays keyed by `(project, entry_paths)` and shared across pulls.
- `compute_update_from_version_operation` is removed; it is no longer used.
- Classification, error propagation and the JS API (`getServerHmrUpdate(from, entryPaths)` and its result) are unchanged.
